DB_5_19.TXT:
Virtual Century: Chronology of the Limited
Wars and VR Development 3
From the turmoil of the eight great plants
to the outbreak of Oratorio Tangram

VCa3 ----------------------
■A fleet led by Colonel Matthew defects
  from the DNA and seizes the 6th Plant,
  "Satchel Mouth" (abbr. SM-06)

■MV-03 completes the Vok series, built
  around the SAV-326 Grys-Vok

■Dr. Yzrman of SM-06 completes
  the RVR-42 Cypher

■SM-06 (Matthew's fleet) storms and
  seizes the 1st Plant,
  "Dancing Under" (abbr. DU-01),
  loots 60% of its stored V-Crystal
  material and withdraws

■The 2nd Plant,
  "Transvaal" (abbr. TV-02),
  completes the RVR-68 Dordray and
  declares priority supply to the RNA

■"The closure of DD-05":
  having sold the HBV-502 Raiden
  in disregard of FR-08,
  DD-05 is driven into closure
  by FR-08's machinations

■The 4th Plant,
  "TSC Drammen" (abbr. TSC),
  completes the SGV-417 Angelan


VCa4 ----------------------
■FR-08 decides on a CA advance
  into SM-06

■SM-06 (Matthew's fleet) makes
  a "defense request" to the RNA

■TSC is found to have diverted Earth
  Crystal material from the South American
  ruins to the RNA

■Tristram Rifaux, head of the Rifaux family,
  is assassinated; FR-08 loses its leader
  and falls into confusion

■Amber IV, missing until now, returns and
  appears at TSC

■Under Amber IV's guidance, TSC expands
  its power, bringing SM-06 and TV-02
  under its wing

■FR-08 installs Lilin Plajiner (age 15)
  as its new leader

■The "Crepuscule" campaign breaks out

■The conflict takes shape: FR-08 (Lilin
  Plajiner), backed by the DNA, against
  TSC (Amber IV), backed by the RNA

■Through statements by Amber IV and
  Lilin Plajiner, the existence of
  "Tangram" and "Bradtos" becomes public

■RP-07 completes the MBV-707 Temjin

■DU-01, TV-02, MV-03, TSC and SM-06
  show signs of defecting from
  the International War Corporation
  and FR-08; to stop this movement,
  the International War Corporation
  and FR-08 propose a planned campaign
  with "Tangram" as its prize

■"Oratorio Tangram" breaks out;
  a great war across the entire Earth
  sphere begins
DB_6_01.TXT:
<Searching for the Enemy: AUTO>
If you lose sight of the enemy, tap the
○ button at once to "turn toward enemy."
With this function, even when the enemy
leaves the screen, you can face it at once.

When the enemy is off-screen, you have no
idea what attack is coming: a very
dangerous situation.
When you lose sight of it, make full use of
"turn toward enemy" and the like to keep
the enemy on screen as much of the time
as possible.

This is the first iron rule of surviving
in combat.
DB_6_02.TXT:
<Ranged Attacks: AUTO>
The □ button is the "attack button."
Just mash it, and the VR's "Support
Control AI" judges your situation and
picks and fires a suitable attack.
At first, don't think; just mash the
□ button when you want to attack.

The △ button is the "strong attack
button." Press it when you want to use
your VR's stronger attacks.

But strong attacks mostly use up a lot
of the weapon gauge. If the gauge lacks
the energy a strong attack needs, a
normal attack fires instead, so watch
the gauge's remaining energy when you
use the strong attack button.


<Key Point for Ranged Attacks>
"Land forward dash attacks!"
Press □ (or △) while dashing for an
attack on the move: a "dash attack."

Dash attacks differ in shot power,
homing and shot count by dash direction.

Remember above all the "dash attack
made while dashing forward."

It is very powerful and can deal great
damage to the enemy.

First, aim to land this forward dash
attack.

Auto-type controls also have a very
handy "Auto Forward Dash Attack."

Dash sideways or diagonally forward,
then press □ with the D-pad neutral.
That alone turns you forward into a
forward dash attack: a superb feature.
With it, countering after dodging an
enemy attack becomes far easier.

Be sure to learn and master it!
DB_6_03.TXT:
<Close-Range Attacks: AUTO>
When the enemy is within close range,
the weapon gauge turns yellow; press the
□ button then to make a "close-range
attack," such as punching the enemy
directly or slashing it with a sword.

Hold the □ button down and up to 3
close-range attacks follow in a row.
(For the Temjin 707S)

Close-range attacks deal heavy damage,
letting you destroy the enemy faster.
But the enemy's close-range attacks deal
heavy damage too. Take one and it will
hurt, so be careful.

Combined with the D-pad, close-range
attacks come in the types below.
Use them as the situation calls for.

"Circling close-range attack"
□ button while holding the D-pad sideways.

"Uppercut close-range attack"
□ button while holding the D-pad back.

"Forward dash close-range attack"
While dashing forward (or diagonally
forward), □ button while holding
the D-pad back.
DB_6_04.TXT:
<Evading Enemy Ranged Attacks: AUTO>
Charge blindly at the enemy and you will
be hit and die in no time.
Mastering how to dodge enemy attacks is
extremely important.
There are many ways to avoid enemy
attacks, but first keep the three below
in mind as you go into battle.

■Dodge No. 1
  "Walk, or dash sideways."
  (To dash, press the D-pad in the
   direction you want, then × button.)

■Dodge No. 2
  "Jump to dodge."
  (To jump, hold the ○ button.)

■Dodge No. 3
  "Dodge with an air dash."
  (To air dash, hold the ○ button to
   jump, and while rising press the
   D-pad in the direction you want.)
DB_6_05.TXT:
<Evading and Countering Enemy Close-Range
Attacks: AUTO>
If the enemy closes in and attacks at close
range, don't panic; deal with it as below.

■Against close-range attacks No. 1
  "Dash out of the enemy's close range."
  (To dash, press the D-pad in the
   direction you want, then × button.)
  ★Get 130 or more away from the enemy!

■Against close-range attacks No. 2
  "Air dash out of the enemy's close
  range."
  (To air dash, hold the ○ button to
   jump, and while rising press the
   D-pad in the direction you want.)
  ★Beware of being hit as you land!

■Against close-range attacks No. 3
  "Guard."
  (If you input nothing, you guard
   automatically.)
  ★Panic costs you. Input nothing!

■Against close-range attacks No. 4
  "Meet it head-on!"
  (For how to make close-range attacks,
   see the separate entry.)
  ★Go ahead, if you're confident!
DB_6_06.TXT:
<Attack and Evasion: Switching Actions:
AUTO> You can't beat the enemy without
attacking. But the more you attack, the more
openings you leave.
Rather than attacking recklessly, judge
when to switch between attack and evasion!

Some enemies can only be damaged at
specific moments.
If your attacks do no damage, focus on
evasion for now, watch for the moment
damage gets through, and attack then.
DB_6_07.TXT:
<Fighting by Distance: AUTO>
In VR combat, controlling your distance
from the enemy is very important.

At long range, you can keep many enemies
on screen at once, enemy moves are easier
to read, and shots take time to arrive,
so they are easier to dodge.

But your own attacks may not reach, or
may deal less damage.

At close range, you can make full use of
many kinds of attack, close-range and
ranged alike, but the closer you get,
the narrower your view becomes, and the
harder it is to sense attacks from other
enemies.

Rather than charging blindly at the
enemy, grasp these merits and demerits
of distance, control your distance from
the enemy, and steer the battle your way.
DB_6_08.TXT:
■To hit the enemy for sure...
Corner the enemy where it can't dodge,
then aim to land your main heavy hitter.

Like your own unit, the enemy is broadly
either "able to evade attacks" or
"unable to evade attacks."

Here we describe how to put the enemy
into the "unable to evade" state.

■When you attack, roughly this happens:
1. The attack hits the enemy directly
2. The enemy evades it, e.g. by dashing
   sideways
3. The enemy evades it by jumping,
   canceling a jump action, etc.
4. Enemy fire cancels out your attack

When the enemy acts as above, it ends up:
1. Somewhat effective; attack further
2. Somewhat effective; the enemy needs
   time for its next move, so attack
   further and corner it
3. Effective; the enemy's next moves are
   limited, so it is predictable, that
   is, easy to target
4. Somewhat effective; the enemy needs
   time for its next move, so attack
   further and corner it

If "somewhat effective," the enemy is a
little harder-pressed to evade than in
its normal stance. Keep attacking and
pile on the pressure to force it into
moves that are harder to evade from,
and land your attack for sure.

If "effective," its options narrow more:
■Land
■Jump attack, then land
■Dash from midair, then land
■Dash attack from midair, then land
It can take only these 4 actions.
Slam your main attack into it as it
lands, and you should almost surely hit.


■Put more simply
Split attacks by purpose into two kinds:
■Harassing attacks
  Low weapon gauge use, small openings;
  better still with good homing
■Main attacks
  Heavy weapon gauge use, big openings;
  ideally heavy damage
Fighting with these, the flow is:
1. Trade harassing attacks and watch for
   openings,
2. corner the enemy so it can't evade,
3. slam in your main attack.


■Understand each unit's armament, keep
the above in mind, and hit the enemy
more efficiently.
DB_6_09.TXT:
■Number of Attacks

■A VR's 3 Weapon Gauges
A VR has 3 weapon gauges: one each for
LW, CW and RW.
By using these gauges in turn, you can
keep attacking without pause.

By attacking without pause, you can pin
the enemy down, forcing it to keep
evading, and hold an offensive stance
that keeps the situation in your favor.


■Using Close-Range Attacks
Close-range attacks use no weapon gauge.
Use this: while the gauges spent on
ranged attacks recover, press in with
close-range attacks, then switch back to
ranged attacks once the gauges recover,
and you can keep attacking the enemy
without pause.


■Canceling Close-Range Attacks
A close-range attack normally swings all
the way through, but there are timings
when a dash, jump, guard, etc. will cut
it short and move you to your next action.

■Example
1. Slash at the enemy with a close-range
   attack
2. Input a dash partway through the slash

The slash is canceled and you instantly
switch to the dash.


By canceling a close-range attack and
chaining into another action, you can
face the enemy without leaving openings,
add more attacks, and respond flexibly
to the situation.

Try it out in many ways and master it!
DB_6_10.TXT:
■Try Switching Units
Depending on the mission, it can be hard
to carry out the operation in your
favorite unit.

Some VRs are highly versatile, while
special-operation VRs specialize in
certain tasks, so carrying out missions
also calls for thinking about using
your units efficiently.

If you hit a hard mission and can't get
past it, try it with various units.


■To Better Understand VR Performance
Each VR is fitted with its own armament.
Flying other units can help you better
grasp the traits of your favorite unit.

You might pick a VR of a similar line,
or one of a completely different line.

By piloting various units, you come to
understand how each differs in mobility,
means of attack, effective tactics and
so on, and by applying what you learn
in one unit to others, you may discover
more effective ways to fight and attack.

You will be issued many kinds of VR, so
board each at least once and try it out.
